subject: ela
skillName: Tell a story or recount an experience

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'I saw a cool animal.'
Description B: 'At the zoo, I watched an octopus change from brown to bright red in about three seconds.'

Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'cool animal' — no name, no location, no action.
Description B names the animal (octopus), the location (zoo), and a specific action (changing color in three seconds).
Description B answers: Where? What animal? What did it do?

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'For the science fair, I grew three bean plants in different amounts of light and measured them every day for four weeks. The one in the most light grew tallest.'
Description B: 'I did a project for the science fair. It was about plants. It turned out pretty good.'

Write A or B.

steps: Description A names the project (bean plants in different light), the method (measured daily), the duration (four weeks), and the result (most light = tallest).
Description B says 'about plants' and 'pretty good' — no useful information.
Description A answers: What did you do? How? How long? What happened?

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions. Which one gives more relevant details?

Description A: 'We went somewhere for vacation. It was fun and we did activities.'
Description B: 'On vacation, my family went snorkeling in a cove and I saw a bright yellow fish swim between my fingers.'

Write A or B.

steps: Description A says 'somewhere' and 'activities' — no specifics at all.
Description B names the activity (snorkeling), the setting (a cove), and a specific vivid moment (yellow fish between fingers).
Description B puts a listener directly into the moment.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions of baking cookies. Both have details, but one has a detail that does not belong.

Description A: 'My grandma and I baked chocolate chip cookies on Saturday. We used two whole bags of chips, so every cookie was extra chocolatey. Cookies are a type of dessert. The kitchen smelled amazing for hours.'

Description B: 'My grandma and I baked chocolate chip cookies on Saturday. We used two whole bags of chips, so every cookie was extra chocolatey. The kitchen smelled amazing for hours.'

Which description is better? Name the detail in the weaker description that does not belong.
items.answer: Description B is better. In Description A, 'Cookies are a type of dessert' does not belong. It is a general fact that adds nothing to this experience. Description B keeps all details focused on what happened during the baking.

steps: Both descriptions open the same way and include the two bags of chips and the smell.
Description A adds: 'Cookies are a type of dessert' — everyone knows this; it is not relevant to this story.
Description B does not include that fact and stays focused on the experience.
Relevant details must connect to the specific experience being described.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions of a soccer game. Both have details, but one has a detail that does not belong.

Description A: 'In our soccer game on Friday, I scored my first goal ever in the last two minutes. My whole team ran over and we jumped in a pile. Soccer is played around the world.'

Description B: 'In our soccer game on Friday, I scored my first goal ever in the last two minutes. My whole team ran over and we jumped in a pile. I could not stop smiling the whole drive home.'

Which description is better? Name the detail in the weaker description that does not belong.
items.answer: Description B is better. In Description A, 'Soccer is played around the world' does not belong. It is a general fact about soccer, not a detail about this game. Description B ends with a personal, relevant detail about how the student felt afterward.

steps: Both descriptions include the goal in the last two minutes and the team celebration.
Description A adds: 'Soccer is played around the world' — a geography/sports fact unrelated to this game.
Description B adds: 'I could not stop smiling the whole drive home' — this shows the emotional impact.
Relevant details stay with the personal experience.

items.prompt:
Read the two descriptions of a visit to a grandparent's house. Both have details, but one has a detail that does not belong.

Description A: 'At my grandpa's house, he showed me his coin collection from fifty years ago. Some coins were from countries that do not even exist anymore. We sat at the kitchen table for two hours looking at each one. Coins are made of metal.'

Description B: 'At my grandpa's house, he showed me his coin collection from fifty years ago. Some coins were from countries that do not even exist anymore. We sat at the kitchen table for two hours looking at each one. He let me pick one to keep.'

Which description is better? Name the detail in the weaker description that does not belong.
items.answer: Description B is better. In Description A, 'Coins are made of metal' does not belong. It is a general fact with no connection to this visit. Description B ends with a meaningful specific detail: the grandfather let the student keep a coin.

steps: Both descriptions include the coin collection, the countries that no longer exist, and two hours at the table.
Description A adds: 'Coins are made of metal' — a basic fact with no relevance to this experience.
Description B adds: 'He let me pick one to keep' — a specific, meaningful outcome of the visit.
Relevant details show what happened during the experience, not general facts about the topic.

items.prompt:
Topic: A time you worked hard on something and it paid off.

Weak description: 'I worked really hard on something at school. It took a long time and I did not give up. In the end I felt good about it.'

What is missing from this description? Write one sentence that adds a specific, relevant detail that would make it stronger.
items.answer: The description is missing what the student worked on, what made it hard, how long it took, and the specific moment it paid off. A better detail: 'I rewrote my story about a dragon three times over two weeks because the ending kept feeling wrong, and when I finally read it aloud to the class, I knew the last sentence was exactly right.'

steps: The weak description says 'something at school' — the listener does not know what it was.
'Took a long time' gives no specific time frame.
'Did not give up' and 'felt good about it' are conclusions without evidence.
Missing details: what the project was, what was hard about it, how many attempts were made, the specific satisfying moment.
A strong added detail names the project and shows the effort and the payoff.

items.prompt:
Topic: The first snow of the year.

Weak description: 'It snowed for the first time this year. We went outside. It was cold and pretty.'

What is missing from this description? Write one sentence that adds a specific, relevant detail that would make it stronger.
items.answer: The description is missing any specific detail about what happened outside, who was there, what it looked and felt like, or a memorable moment. A better detail: 'My little brother had never seen snow before, and when the first flake landed on his mitten he stared at it so hard and so quietly that I held my breath waiting for him to say something.'

steps: The weak description says 'went outside' with no description of what happened.
'Cold and pretty' could describe any snow ever — no specific detail.
Missing details: who was there, what they did, a specific sensory or emotional moment.
A strong added detail captures one specific moment that makes the snow day memorable.
Example: 'I lay down in the yard and made a snow angel, and when I stood up the shape was perfect except for my boot print right in the middle.'
